Check the car\'s date
The car says the phone\'s certificate isn\'t valid on its date. Set the car\'s clock, then plug in again.
Unexpected answer
The car answered the certificate check with code %1$s.
The car refused the picture
The car wouldn\'t open its screen to myCar (code %1$s).
No picture for the car
The phone\'s video encoder wouldn\'t start (%1$s). myCar closed the connection: connect again.
The car\'s picture stopped
The phone\'s video encoder keeps failing (%1$s). myCar closed the connection: connect again.
The car didn\'t answer
The connection opened but the car sent nothing. If Android asks which app to open for the car, choose myCar.
The car hung up during setup
The car ended the connection while securing it. This usually means it turned down the certificate.
The car hung up after the certificate
The car accepted the certificate but ended the connection before setup was done.

Bluetooth permission missing
myCar needs the Nearby devices permission to reach %1$s. Allow it in the app\'s settings, then try again.
Couldn\'t publish the Android Auto service
Car didn\'t connect over Bluetooth
%1$s didn\'t open Android Auto with the phone. Check that wireless Android Auto is on in the car\'s settings, then reconnect the phone from the car\'s Bluetooth menu.
Couldn\'t join the car\'s Wi-Fi
Android didn\'t connect to %1$s\'s network. If a \"Connect to device\" prompt appeared, it has to be accepted.
A VPN is blocking the car

myCar joined %1$s\'s network, but a VPN on this phone (Tailscale, for one) won\'t let it reach the car. Connect with the cable, turn the VPN off, or leave myCar out of it in its settings - then Plancia and Xonos inside myCar can\'t use the VPN\'s addresses, like Tailscale names.
